sources.citation: Fleck, David W. 2013. Panoan languages and linguistics. Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History 99. New York: AMNH.
sources.note: Nothing about this variety's stress. Classifies †Kashinawa of the Tarauacá River as an 'independent member of Nawa Group' (Table 1, II.C.iv; p. 17 table) distinct from Kashinawa of the Ibuaçu River [cbs]; the appendix of documentation (p. 97) gives the entire record as 'Tastevin (ms. c) 144-entry lexicon; partial reproductions: 125 entries in Tastevin ms. b; 128 entries in Rivet and Tastevin (1927–1929, 1932)'; table 6 (p. 35) gives 129 items for it. The family-level phonology section (pp. 43–44) discusses only proto-Panoan inventory and tone in Chakobo/Kapanawa/Amawaka, with no stress statem…
sources.venue: Anthropological Papers of the American Museum of Natural History

sources.citation: Christino, Beatriz Protti. 2012. [Review of] Cunha, Manuela Carneiro da (org.) (2009). Tastevin, Parrissier: Fontes sobre índios e seringueiros do Alto Juruá. Rio de Janeiro: Museu do Índio – FUNAI (Série Monografias). LIAMES: Línguas Indígenas Americanas 12: 195-197 (pp.). DOI 10.20396/liames.v0i12.1490.
sources.note: No phonology content. The reviewer notes the volume mentions vocabulary collecting only anecdotally (a Kapanawa vocabulary from a woman on the rio Tejo, p. 68; Waninawa collecting, p. 119) and states 'Tastevin não chegou a dominar as línguas indígenas que documentou e tampouco a reunir narrativas tradicionais nessas línguas' -- confirming there is no linguistic description by Tastevin beyond the wordlists.

sources.citation: Rivet, Paul & Constant Tastevin. 1927. Les dialectes Pano du haut Juruá et du haut Purus (part 1). Anthropos 22: 811–827.
sources.note: Nothing. The paper is a comparative wordlist; pp. 811–819 (intro, bibliography, remarks) read in full and the whole article a full-text search for stress/accent/tonique/prosod with no hit. Tastevin's 'Kašinawa' (= this variety, siglum 3') appears only as list forms (e.g. tatû-unga 'canot', tibo-ra, tô-ra); the only phonetic remark is that initial r > d in de Abreu's and Tastevin's Kašinawa (p. 818). The authors note (p. 818) that Tastevin's Kašinawa is 'le plus aberrant des trois' Kašinawa lists and that the dialect must have split into sub-dialects.

sources.note: No phonology content; itinerary, ethnonyms (Papavo, Katayana, Hu-nawa) and a pointer to La Géographie 43-45 for the ethnographic notes.
sources.venue: Journal de la Société des Américanistes

sources.citation: Tastevin, Constant. 1926. Le haut Tarauacá. La Géographie (Paris) 45: 34-54, 158-175.
sources.note: No phonology content. The only remark on pronunciation is footnote 1 on p. 40 (Gallica view 51): 'L'e sans accent des mots Kachinaux reproduits dans cet article doivent se prononcer même à la fin des mots exactement comme l'e muet français des mots je, me, ne, de.' -- an orthographic note ('accent' = written diacritic), nothing on word stress or tone. Whole-volume full-text search: 'tonique' 0 hits in the article, 'syllabe' 0, 'prononc' only 'la vraie prononciation est Papaho, qu'on prononce en soufflant le h' (p. 50).
